title: JavaScript creation and early naming history (Mocha, LiveScript, JavaScript) with verified sources
learningObjectives: Explain javascript creation and early naming history (mocha, livescript, javascript) with verified sources and describe JavaScript's role in web development.

understand.concept: JavaScript was created by Brendan Eich at Netscape in 1995. It was initially developed under the name Mocha, then called LiveScript, and later JavaScript as part of a marketing arrangement. JavaScript is not the same language as Java. Its standardised language specification is ECMAScript.
understand.whyItMatters: Knowing the naming history prevents the common misconception that JavaScript is a dialect of Java. Historical details should be sourced carefully and separated from modern language standards.
understand.analogy: A product name can change during a project's history; the current name does not necessarily describe its technical relationship to another product.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; language standards and host runtime APIs have precise technical boundaries.

explain.narrative: The example is a browser script. The historical names describe the language's early development, not different modern languages learners must use.
